source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
The guide describes propagating banana from corm pieces rather than seed. A healthy corm is dug up about 4 days after cutting down the parent stem, then cut into pieces, each piece carrying at least one viable "eye" (bud, labeled in the source's diagram but not confidently transcribed here - see the open items note in this batch's handover) capable of sprouting; eyes are visible as small raised points on the corm surface. Corm pieces are typically cut to roughly a fist-sized piece per eye.

Cut corm pieces should be soaked or treated in a fungicide/disinfectant solution (shown in the source as a pink-colored dip) for a short period to protect against rot and soil-borne disease before planting. Treated pieces are planted into a nursery bed and kept there for about 15 to 20 days until shoots emerge, then transplanted into individual planting bags. After roughly 10 more days in bags, seedlings develop several true leaves and are ready to be hardened off and transplanted to the field.
